newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EMU jitters, crown drive Swedish bond yields up.
newsitem.headline: EMU jitters, crown drive Swedish bond yields up.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended higher on Monday on continued speculation that Europe's monetary union would be delayed.
Statements by German central bank head Hans Tietmeyer and European Monetary Institute president Alexandre Lamfalussy that the project was on track were not enough to quell market fears, dealers said.
"The climate is speculative. The market wants to test EMU," one dealer said.
Dealers said the weakness of the crown was also driving yields up.

The soft crown would probably block a cut in the Riksbank's key repurchase rate from its current level of 4.10 percent. The market was expecting the Riksbank to keep rates unchanged on Tuesday, a Reuter survey showed.
The market focus was on a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday, German unemployment on Thursday and U.S. jobs data on Friday.

The crown weakened to 4.4855 crowns to the mark versus 4.4340 on Friday. Six month T-bill rate rose four basis points to 4.21 percent and ten year bond yield rose seven basis points to 6.86 percent. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
